subject: Post-call: LatticePoint inference fit & action items
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.k@latticepoint.ai>, Marco Diaz <m.diaz@latticepoint.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@latticepoint.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: LatticePoint inference fit & action items

Aisha / Marco — thanks again for the 45‑minute demo and honest discussion today. Short summary of what I heard and proposed next steps so we're aligned before the technical deep‑dive.

Key pain points (your words):
- Cost at scale: inference token spend and instance hours are outpacing forecasts as ML usage grows.
- Latency spikes under concurrent traffic (esp. batch processing at 10am PST).
- Data residency & encryption: logs and traces must remain within US regions; PII redaction requirements.

Primary goals:
- P95 inference latency target: <= 200 ms for short (<=128 token) responses; tail behavior under 95th percentile critical.
- Sustained throughput: 500–700 concurrent inference requests during peak, with burst handling to ~1,000 for short windows.
- Predictable unit economics: options to reduce per‑token cost (quantization, batching, prefix caching) without regression in NLU accuracy.

Model constraints you mentioned:
- Primary model: LatticePoint intends to run an open LLM (70B class) with gen quality comparable to LLaMA‑style baselines; quantization to 4‑bit is acceptable with a small eval set to validate accuracy.
- KV cache warm‑up: cold‑start latency visible on sudden traffic ramps.

Immediate asks / next steps I proposed on the call:
1) Send over a short token distribution sample and a recent traffic day (UTC timestamps) — helps sizing and batch tuning. (Action: Aisha)
2) Schedule a 90‑minute technical deep‑dive next week with one of our Solutions Engineers to walk model I/O, expected sequence lengths, and topology recommendations. (Action: Camila / Ben)
3) I attached an initial sizing workbook with a rough Dedicated vs Private cost sketch — we'll refine after we see token & concurrency samples. (Attachment: initial-sizing.xlsx)

Proposed agenda for deep‑dive:
- Clarify 95/99 latency SLOs and acceptable tradeoffs
- Token length distribution, top prompt patterns
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC in us‑central vs Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity
- Quantization & accuracy guardrails, eval plan
- Rollout and fallback policies (model variants, region fallbacks)

If that aligns, can you confirm availability for a deep‑dive 09/20 or 09/21? Once you confirm times, I'll send a calendar invite and include the Solutions Engineer and an infra architect.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
(415) 555‑0148

Attachment: initial-sizing.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.k@latticepoint.ai>

Cc: Marco Diaz <m.diaz@latticepoint.ai>, procurement <procurement@latticepoint.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 17:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LatticePoint inference fit & action items

Thanks Camila — that matches our notes. A few clarifications and answers:

- Token/sample data: I'll pull a 48‑hour sample (anonymized) and a CSV of request timestamps — expect that by EOD Monday (09/20). (Action: Aisha)
- Concurrency: our internal dashboards show ~580 sustained concurrent RPS at peak with short bursts up to ~1,100 for 10–15 minutes.
- Sequence lengths: median ~60 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens; a lot of short prompts with occasional long context for document summarization.
- Compliance: primary requirement is US‑only for production inference and audit logs. We'll need Redwoods to support KMS integration for encryption at rest.

Procurement is copied; they will need a preliminary SOW and an estimated monthly committed cost range to start internal approval. (Procurement: please advise preferred SOW template.)

09/20 works best for us in the afternoon (PST). Prefer 90 minutes so we can do a live model run. Thanks — looking forward to the deep‑dive.

—Aisha
Aisha Kumar
Head of AI Infrastructure, LatticePoint
aisha.k@latticepoint.ai
